procedures.title: ENGINE FAILURE - ALTITUDE ABOVE 450 FEET
procedures.conditions: Engine failure at altitude above 450 feet
steps: Lower collective pitch.
Enter normal autorotation.
Establish a steady glide of 52kt (60 mph) IAS approximately.
At an altitude of approximately 50 feet, initiate a flare.
At approximately 10 feet, coordinate collective pitch with forward movement of cyclic stick to level aircraft and cushion landing. Make ground contact with aircraft level.
Avoid rapid lowering of collective pitch or the use of aft cyclic stick during initial ground contact or during ground slide.
In the event of engine failure at night, do not turn on landing light above 1,000 feet above terrain in order to preserve battery power.

procedures.title: ENGINE FAILURE - ALTITUDE ABOVE 7 FEET AND BELOW 450 FEET
procedures.conditions: Conduct takeoff operations in accordance with the restrictions shown on Height Velocity Diagram (Figure 5-2). Engine failure during takeoff at altitude above 7 feet and below 450 feet.
steps: Lower the collective pitch (altitude permitting), in order to maintain rotor speed.
The amount and duration of collective reduction depends upon the height above the ground at which the engine failure occurs.
As the ground is approached, use aft cyclic and collective as needed to decrease forward and vertical velocity.
Establish a level attitude prior to ground contact.
Apply collective pitch as necessary in order to cushion landing.

procedures.title: ENGINE FAILURE - ALTITUDE BELOW 7 FEET
procedures.conditions: A power failure is indicated by a sudden yawing of the ship to the left.
steps: Do not reduce collective pitch.
Apply right pedal to prevent excessive yawing and right stick to minimize drift.
Apply collective pitch as necessary in order to cushion landing.

procedures.title: DITCHING - POWER OFF
procedures.conditions: Follow the procedures defined in paragraphs 3-1 through 3-3 for autorotation approach and landing. Upon contact with water, proceed as follows:
steps: Lower collective pitch and apply sideward cyclic stick after contact is made with water.
Release seat belt and shoulder harness.
Open both doors and exit helicopter.
warnings: CLEAR HELICOPTER IMMEDIATELY TO PREVENT INJURY.

procedures.title: DITCHING - POWER ON
steps: Descend to hovering altitude over water.
Unlatch doors.
Passenger exit aircraft.
Fly a safe distance away.
Turn battery and alternator switches OFF.
Close twistgrip to idle position.
Allow aircraft to settle in a level attitude, apply full collective.
When aircraft begins to roll, reduce collective to full down.
Release seat belt and shoulder harness.
When rotor blades have stopped turning, clear aircraft as quickly as possible.

procedures.title: TRANSMISSION WARNING/CAUTION INDICATORS
steps: Main Rotor Transmission - Transmission Oil Temperature and Pressure: A red warning light (M/R XMSN TEMP/PRESS) on the instrument panel comes on when transmission oil pressure drops below 2-1/2 psi or temperature exceeds 235°F.
Land as soon as possible if light comes on in flight.

Optional Chip Detector Caution Indicator (If Installed): An amber caution light (M/R XMSN CHIPS) on the instrument panel comes on to indicate possible deterioration of components within the main rotor transmission.
Land as soon as possible if light comes on in flight.

Tail Rotor Transmission - Chip Detector Caution Indicator: An amber caution light (T/R XMSN CHIPS) on the instrument panel comes on to indicate possible deterioration of components within the tail rotor transmission.
Land as soon as possible if light comes on in flight.

procedures.title: FUEL LOW, CAUTION INDICATOR
steps: An amber fuel low caution light (FUEL LOW) on the instrument panel comes on in flight when approximately one gallon of usable fuel remains in the tank.
If fuel low caution light comes on during flight, land immediately.
warnings: Do not use fuel low caution light as a working indication of fuel quantity (flight time remaining).

procedures.title: CLUTCH WARNING LIGHT
steps: A red clutch warning light (RELEASE) is illuminated whenever the clutch is not fully engaged.
Be prepared to enter autorotation.
Land as soon as possible if clutch warning light comes on in flight.

procedures.title: TAIL ROTOR FAILURE
procedures.conditions: Different types of failure may require slightly different techniques for optimum success in recovery.
steps: General Corrective Action - Complete loss of tail rotor thrust: Failure is normally indicated by an uncontrollable (by pedal) yawing to the right.
In Forward Flight - Reduce power by lowering collective.
In Forward Flight - Adjust airspeed to 50 to 60 knots.
In Forward Flight - Use left lateral cyclic in combination with collective pitch to limit left sideslip to a reasonable angle.

In Forward Flight - If conditions permit, place the twistgrip in the IDLE position once a landing area is selected, and perform a normal autorotation. Plan to touch down with little or no forward speed.
While at a hover: Place the twistgrip in the IDLE position and perform a hovering autorotation.
Tail Rotor Control Failure - Fixed Pitch Setting: Adjust power to maintain 50 to 60 knots airspeed.

Tail Rotor Control Failure - Fixed Pitch Setting: Perform a shallow approach and running landing to a suitable area, touching down into wind at a speed between effective translational lift and 30 knots. Directional control may be accomplished by small adjustments in throttle and/or collective control.
warnings: WHEN HOVERING AT ALTITUDES WITHIN OR ABOVE THE CROSS-HATCHED AREAS DEPICTED ON THE HEIGHT VELOCITY DIAGRAM (FIG. 5-2), IT IS NECESSARY TO REDUCE ALTITUDE TO 7 FEET OR LESS PRIOR TO PLACING THE TWISTGRIP IN THE GROUND IDLE POSITION AND PERFORMING A HOVERING AUTOROTATION.

procedures.title: ENGINE IDLE AT ALTITUDE
procedures.conditions: Engine idle speeds at high density altitudes may be less than those set at sea level conditions.
steps: Do not rapidly reduce throttle to idle stop in flight.
warnings: TO MINIMIZE POSSIBILITY OF ENGINE STOPPAGE, RAPID THROTTLE REDUCTIONS TO FULL IDLE DURING FLIGHT SHALL NOT BE CONDUCTED AT ANY ALTITUDE.

procedures.title: AIR RESTART
steps: Establish 52 kt (60 mph) autorotation.
Pick out landing spot. If less than 2000 feet above terrain, proceed with autorotation landing.
If altitude permits (Helicopters with carbureted engine - HO-360-C1A): Mixture - FULL RICH
If altitude permits (Helicopters with carbureted engine - HO-360-C1A): Throttle - CRACK APPROXIMATELY 1/2 AN INCH
If altitude permits (Helicopters with carbureted engine - HO-360-C1A): Starter - ENGAGE
If altitude permits (Helicopters with fuel injected engine - HIO-360-G1A): Mixture - IDLE CUT OFF
If altitude permits (Helicopters with fuel injected engine - HIO-360-G1A): Throttle - CRACK APPROXIMATELY 1/2 AN INCH
If altitude permits (Helicopters with fuel injected engine - HIO-360-G1A): Starter - ENGAGE
If altitude permits (Helicopters with fuel injected engine - HIO-360-G1A): Mixture push to FULL RICH when engine fires.
warnings: If fuel pump was on at time of engine stoppage, a flooded condition may have resulted necessitating additional use of the starter.

procedures.title: ENGINE/FUSELAGE/ELECTRICAL FIRE ON THE GROUND
steps: Mixture - IDLE CUTOFF (Pull)
Fuel valve - CLOSE (Pull)
Battery - OFF
Alternator - OFF
Exit aircraft with fire extinguisher
Extinguish fire
warnings: REMAIN CLEAR OF ROTOR BLADES DURING AND AFTER EVACUATION.

procedures.title: ENGINE/FUSELAGE FIRE, OR FIRE OF UNDETERMINED ORIGIN, IN FLIGHT - LOW/CRUISE ALTITUDE (Power-On Landing)
procedures.conditions: If a fire is observed during flight, prevailing conditions such as day/night, altitude, and available landing areas must be considered in order to determine whether to execute a power-on or power-off landing.
steps: Maintain airspeed and rotor RPM; be prepared to perform a full autorotation at any point in the approach.
Immediately perform power-on landing to suitable area.
If time permits: Battery - OFF
If time permits: Alternator - OFF
If time permits: Cabin Heater - OFF
Upon landing: Throttle - CLOSE
Upon landing: Mixture - IDLE CUTOFF (Pull)
Upon landing: Fuel valve - CLOSE (Pull)
Upon landing: Exit aircraft with fire extinguisher
Upon landing: Extinguish fire

procedures.title: ENGINE/FUSELAGE FIRE, OR FIRE OF UNDETERMINED ORIGIN, IN FLIGHT - LOW/CRUISE ALTITUDE (Power-Off Landing)
procedures.conditions: If a fire is observed during flight, prevailing conditions such as day/night, altitude, and available landing areas must be considered in order to determine whether to execute a power-on or power-off landing.
steps: Immediately enter autorotation.
If time permits: Mixture - IDLE CUTOFF (Pull)
If time permits: Fuel valve - CLOSE (Pull)
If time permits: Battery - OFF
If time permits: Alternator - OFF
If time permits: Cabin Heater - OFF
Upon landing: Exit aircraft with fire extinguisher.
Upon landing: Extinguish fire.

procedures.title: ELECTRICAL FIRE - IN FLIGHT
steps: Battery - OFF
Alternator - OFF
Immediately perform power-on landing to suitable area.
Upon landing: Throttle - CLOSE
Upon landing: Mixture - IDLE CUTOFF (Pull)
Upon landing: Fuel valve - CLOSE (Pull)
Upon landing: Exit aircraft with fire extinguisher.
Upon landing: Extinguish fire.

procedures.title: SMOKE AND FUME ELIMINATION - IN FLIGHT
procedures.conditions: Smoke and/or toxic fumes entering the cockpit can be exhausted as follows:
steps: Open vents.
Adjust cabin heat and defog handle, as required.
Land as soon as possible.

procedures.title: THROTTLE FAILURE - IN FLIGHT
procedures.conditions: If the throttle becomes inoperative in flight
steps: Continue to a landing area that will permit a shallow approach and running landing.
As descent is begun, make collective pitch adjustments smoothly and minimize the amount of movement to aid in maintaining RPM within limits.

If descent cannot be made without an excessively high RPM, fly to a suitable area and accomplish an autorotational landing. In this situation, the mixture control must be moved to the lean position before the collective pitch is lowered to enter autorotation.
If the throttle fails at a hover, lower the collective (disregarding engine RPM) and land.
After the helicopter is on the ground, move the mixture control to the lean position.
